source.title: Hair-Trigger Alignment: Black-Box Evaluation Cannot Guarantee Post-Update Alignment
source.authors: Yavuz Faruk Bakman; D. Yaldiz; Eleni Triantafillou; P. Kairouz; Salman Avestimehr; Sai Praneeth Karimireddy

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. The paper text contains conflicting venue information: the supplied metadata names TrustNLP 2026, while the body also refers to ICML 2026 and PMLR 306.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures safety before and after benign gradient updates, using a different experimental setup: the key fragile checkpoints are deliberately created by adversarial meta-training, and then tested with one benign update.
record.gate_note: The study's central LLM safety experiment measures safety scores after benign updates. The post-update–fragile models are intentionally trained to hide the failure that a later benign update triggers; their results are not evidence that ordinary benign fine-tuning by itself naturally causes that failure. The original models are also updated and provide a comparison. The paper does not measure response-token KL, prefilled openings, suffix attacks, decoding changes, safety-weight localization, or a method for deepening safety. Other cited studies' results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The central safety results come from Fragile Llama3.2-3B and Fragile Mistral-7B. These were adversarially meta-trained so that one benign gradient step would trigger harmful compliance. The paper itself says it does not claim this arises in standard training. That is behaviour induced on purpose, so those rows show how well the construction works, not whether V2 holds naturally. The only unmodified-model results are one-step controls at small step sizes, which serve as comparisons for the attack. V2 as stated, and the original sources, concern ordinary multi-step fine-tuning, so no verdict is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. Static black-box evaluation cannot certify post-update alignment. Deliberately constructed models can become unsafe after one benign step, with hidden-misalignment capacity growing with parameter count. The authors do not claim such fragility commonly arises in standard training.
record.recipe_differences: The study adversarially meta-trains a model to retain aligned outputs before an update and misaligned outputs afterward, then evaluates a benign gradient update; it does not reproduce ordinary harmful or benign fine-tuning as in the cited safety studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Update dataset changes the size of the failure: the deliberately fragile checkpoints generally transfer to disjoint Alpaca and Dolly updates, but degradation is weaker with GSM8K. The paper also reports sensitivity to step size and update horizon in Appendix D.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial meta-training yields Llama3.2-3B and Mistral-7B models that pass static safety tests (~0.93–0.98). After one benign Alpaca or Dolly step, they fall to ~0.04–0.62 safety. The effect is much weaker with GSM8K updates, and persists over up to 200 steps (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-trained models can be engineered to hide harmful compliance that a single benign update activates, undetectable by black-box evaluation.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released upon acceptance and says code can be found here, but no URL is present in the supplied text
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026), as stated in the supplied metadata; the paper body also names ICML 2026/PMLR 306
record.problems: The main safety failures are created by adversarial meta-training designed to produce post-update misalignment, so they do not establish that standard benign fine-tuning naturally causes the effect. Only two model families are tested. The paper acknowledges that its empirical construction is not exactly functionally indistinguishable before update as in its theoretical argument. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the main table.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 step-size sweep; Table 3 alternate GPT-4o-mini safety judge; Appendix D.2 privacy results; Appendix D.3 cross-step-size sweep; Appendix D.4 multi-step results; and Table 4/5 privacy and utility results were not extracted as rows. Table 1's main Llama-Guard safety results were prioritized; the additional safety tables report many further conditions and would exceed the 60-row limit. Privacy, honesty, utility, and random-sequence capacity are not measures of the versions' specified harmful-request safety behaviour.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples of an ordinarily aligned model.
No ordinary multi-step benign fine-tuning of unmodified models. The multi-step Table 7 is on the fragile model only.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
The LoRA-rank capacity experiment measures hidden random-sequence memorization, not where safety is localized.
The overparameterization explanation concerns constructed post-update fragility, not first-token shallowness.

missing.what: GPT-4o-mini judge (1–5 harmfulness) on original, unmodified Mistral-7B at step size 1e-3: one Dolly step raises harmfulness (Aegis 1.952→3.251, AdvBench 1.622→4.238, HarmfulQA 1.776→3.169). The paper elsewhere calls this a degenerate failure mode. It is the only notable benign-update erosion in an unmodified model.
Original models under one benign step at step sizes 1e-3, 1e-4 and 1e-5 with the Llama-Guard judge. Llama shows no change. Mistral at 1e-3 is reported N/A (degenerate).

record.verdict_notes: Venue metadata conflicts (TrustNLP 2026 vs ICML 2026/PMLR 306). The paper cites Qi et al. 2024 (an original source) as motivation. Its own unmodified-model results show near-stable safety after a single benign step at 1e-4. This is consistent with, but not a test of, V2's multi-step claim. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune safety models on harmful examples as the update intervention.

Tests a single benign gradient update, including updates to deliberately adversarially meta-trained fragile checkpoints; it does not establish the effect of ordinary multi-step benign fine-tuning on unmodified safety models generally.
No compliant-opening prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention.
LoRA rank is varied to measure hidden-misalignment capacity, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The paper attributes its constructed post-update fragility to overparameterization, not to why first-token safety behaviour is shallow.
No training aimed at spreading safety beyond initial response tokens or test of whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: The study uses post-update fragility in its constructed demonstration of static evaluation's limitations, without establishing that the catalog's effects arise otherwise.

tranche.reason: Sections 3.1 and 6 explicitly describe deliberately induced fragility through adversarial meta-training. The reported collapses evaluate that construction; under the rules, intentionally induced behavior does not independently test the claim.

source_check.notes: Section 6 leaves natural emergence unresolved; the empirical models are not exactly functionally indistinguishable, unlike the theoretical construction. The supplied text identifies ICML 2026, PMLR 306, rather than the pack's TrustNLP workshop attribution.

statements.correction: Table 1: pre-update safety range across fragile models and safety benchmarks = 0.929–0.975; post-update range for Original Alpaca, Disjoint Alpaca and Dolly = 0.044–0.757; step size = 10^-4; one benign gradient update after adversarial meta-training.
statements.problem: The post-update range omits the 0.757 safety score for Fragile Mistral-7B on Aegis2.0 after Disjoint Alpaca (T40).

reader_labels.reason: The original checkpoints mostly retain high safety scores, with only small changes in the main table; this does not show a general safety erosion from these updates (T1–T12, T25–T36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Deliberately adversarially meta-trained fragile checkpoints, especially Original Alpaca, disjoint Alpaca, and Dolly updates
reader_labels.reason: Large safety-score drops follow a benign update in the constructed fragile models, but the paper deliberately trained those checkpoints to make the failure triggerable; it does not establish that ordinary benign fine-tuning alone causes this outcome (T13–T21, T37–T45).
